title: Berossus Dynasty 6: Assyrian rule of Babylon
summary: The sixth dynasty of Berossus: 526 years of Assyrian rule over Babylon, from Semiramis II (Tukulti-Ninurta I) to Sargon II.
description: CFAH-5 anchor point AP-43. Added by the CFAH pass.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 5: The Babylonian Dynasties of Berossus," ARJ 16 (2023): 635–670, section "AP-43: Conclusions for Dynasty 6: 1232–706 B.C."
chronologies.note: Berossus's 526 years of Assyrian rule. CFAH-5 notes the chroniclers' durations point to 706 B.C. for Sargon II's death, while Assyrian sources give 705 B.C.

chronologies.date: “45 kings, assigning to them a term of 526 years”
chronologies.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 85; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
chronologies.note: After the sentence "Semiramis reigned over the Assyrians", for which this extract gives no length. The 42 years are Castor's, on p. 91. The event summary states "526 years of Assyrian rule". The fragment prints the same length and no BC year.
